answer: Require every new agent to finish a 72-hour proof-of-uptime before it can trade. The network issues a unique puzzle seed; the agent must crunch it continuously, sending a heartbeat every ten minutes, and more than two missed beats reset the clock to zero. One identity therefore costs three full days of machine time, so a farm aiming for 1,000 fake agents must burn 72,000 GPU-hours, about $36,000 at $0.50 per hour. Like shale hardening slowly under pressure, the wait makes cheap copies heavy, and a plume of fakes cannot flood the harbor when each must first survive the long tide alone.
